meta.title: In Spring — Vocabulary Set 5
meta.subject: English Vocabulary
meta.description: Challenge quiz on word families, antonyms, synonyms, and parts of speech for 'In Spring'.

questions.question: Which of these is the opposite (antonym) of 'warmth'?
questions.explanation: 'Coldness' is the opposite of 'warmth' (which is the feeling of heat).

questions.question: 'Breeze' is a noun, and 'breezy' is its adjective form.
questions.explanation: True. 'Breeze' is the noun (a gentle wind), and 'breezy' describes a windy day (adjective).

questions.question: Which word is a synonym for 'spy' in the sentence 'spy flowers hiding'?
questions.explanation: To 'spy' means to notice, see, or catch sight of something.

questions.question: The words 'link' and 'separate' are synonyms.
questions.explanation: False. 'Link' (to connect) and 'separate' (to pull apart) are antonyms.

questions.question: Which word can act as both a noun (a hand movement) and a verb (to move your hand)?
questions.explanation: 'Wave' can be the action (to wave good-bye) or the thing (a wave of hand or water).

questions.question: 'Struggle' is a verb. Its form that describes currently making a difficult effort is _______.
questions.explanation: The present participle of 'struggle' is 'struggling,' like fawns struggling to walk.

questions.question: In the phrase 'young legs,' what part of speech is 'young'?
questions.explanation: 'Young' is an adjective because it describes the noun 'legs' (what age they are).

questions.question: Sort these words into Verbs (action words) or Nouns (naming words):
questions.explanation: 'Blow' and 'dart' describe actions (verbs). 'Breeze,' 'coat,' and 'tadpole' are names of things (nouns).

questions.question: The word 'groundless' (having no reason) belongs to the 'ground' word family.
questions.explanation: True. 'Groundless' uses the suffix '-less' on the root word 'ground' (base/reason).

questions.question: Arrange the words to describe a breezy day:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'The day was very breezy.' 'Breezy' is the adjective form of 'breeze.'

questions.question: In the sentence 'Worms coil up,' what part of speech is 'coil'?
questions.explanation: Here, 'coil' is a verb describing the action of the worms winding their bodies.

questions.question: The adjective form of the noun 'warmth' is _______.
questions.explanation: 'Warm' describes the weather or feeling, while 'warmth' is the noun.

questions.question: Arrange the words to define a link:
questions.explanation: Correct sentence: 'A link connects things together.' This is its function.

questions.question: The word 'baby' can act as both a noun (the baby chick) and an adjective describing something young (baby fawns).
questions.explanation: True. 'Baby' is a noun when it stands alone, but in 'baby fawns' it acts as an adjective describing fawns.

questions.question: Which word family includes the word 'breeze'?
questions.explanation: All of these words are formed from the base word 'breeze' and are part of the same word family.
